reforms.description: The federal government announced an additional C$1.3 billion programme for science and technology over the next five years, aimed at enhancing research and innovation capacity. This includes a proposal to double the C$250 million spent on job training under the unemployment insurance programme, along with additional funding for existing programmes addressing skill shortages and measures to encourage R&D to boost competitiveness.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The funding aims to enhance research and innovation capacity, which is expected to boost competitiveness and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government announced an additional C$1.3 billion programme.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a significant increase in funding for science and technology, which is important for enhancing R&D capacity.
reforms.source_quote: However, it proposed a doubling of the C$250 million spent on job training under the unemployment insurance programme, C$300 million more for existing programmes dealing with skill shortages, a new training tax and tax concessions to promote private sector worker training, national standards for redundancy notice and minimum severance pay, as well as measures to encourage R&D to boost competitiveness.

reforms.description: The Canadian government introduced a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms as part of its efforts to rationalize the tax and grant system for research and development.
reforms.component_name: R&D Tax Credit for Small Firms
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The tax credit is designed to incentivize small firms to invest in R&D, thereby fostering innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canadian government introduced a refundable R&D tax credit.
reforms.importance_rationale: The introduction of a refundable R&D tax credit is a significant reform aimed at supporting small firms in their research efforts.
reforms.source_quote: Introduced refundable R&D tax credit for small firms.
